ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, AD is the median on the base BC of the isosceles $\triangle ABC$, BE bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects AD at point E. Given $AC=12$ and $DE=3$, what is the area of $\triangle ABE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line EF $\perp$ AD at point F, \\
since AD is the median of the base BC of the isosceles $\triangle ABC$, \\
therefore EF $\perp$ AB, \\
since BE bisects $\angle ABC$, \\
therefore EF=ED=3, \\
therefore $S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot EF=\frac{1}{2}\times 12\times 3=\boxed{18}$.

Reasoning: Because triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle with BC as the base, the two legs are equal, AB=AC=12. The median AD on the base of an isosceles triangle is also perpendicular to the base BC, so DE is along AD, and D is on BC, so DE=3 is the perpendicular distance from point E to side BC. Also because E is on the angle bisector BE of ∠ABC, the perpendicular distances from a point on an angle bisector to the two sides BA and BC of the angle are equal, so the perpendicular distance from point E to side BA is also equal to 3. Taking AB as the base of triangle ABE, AB=12, and the corresponding height is 3, therefore the area is (1/2)×12×3=18.
